description:
## Problem
Upstream sqlglot (main 0c79658d, after v30.35.0) writes correct SQLite SQL for MySQL `SELECT CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL 90 DAY` (`DATE(CURRENT_DATE, '-90 DAY')`) but also reports "SQLite DATE() may discard the time in interval arithmetic". With unsupported_level=RAISE that is an error, so strict callers reject valid queries. PostgreSQL `d >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3' MONTH` behaves the same. CURRENT_DATE has no time part, so the warning is a false positive. The fork fixes it in the carried patch sqlite-date-interval-arithmetic (sqlglot/generators/sqlite.py, the exp.CurrentDate base check near line 642).

## Change
File a tobymao/sqlglot issue (upstream accepts PRs only from collaborators) that shows the false positive and links a fork commit containing only the upstream-relevant change: treat an exp.CurrentDate base as DATE in SQLite interval arithmetic, with tests in tests/dialects/test_sqlite.py that run on real SQLite.

## Guardrails
- Owner approved this offer on 2026-11-26 (choice dialog). Post only this offer.
- Title in Conventional Commits form ending with [CLAUDE]; no fork-only behaviour or benchbox references.
- The fork patch stays carried until upstream merges a fix and a refresh retires the CURRENT_DATE rule with equivalence evidence.
